newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Thieves nab New Zealand TV star Sweetie the rat.
newsitem.headline: Thieves nab New Zealand TV star Sweetie the rat.

text.p: The rodent star of a soon-to-be-released international television series has been stolen, owners of the film company said on Wednesday.
Sweetie the rat vanished when burglars ransacked the Gibson Group film production company in Wellington.
Sweetie stars in the latest instalments of Mirror Mirror, a children's fantasy series.
"Sweetie is a star. She is an important character ...," said art department co-ordinator Heidi Oosterman.
The specially-trained white and fawn rat had been depressed recently, rarely leaving her bed, and Oosterman said: "Something like this could devastate her."
Thieves also stole a stereo, computers, CDs, a toaster and cellphones but staff just want Sweetie back. They are mystified about the thieves' motivation in taking the rat.
"She is cute. She is not your everyday normal-looking rat. They didn't steal her food and I'm worried she will go hungry."
Staff would be scouring pet shops for a stand-in for the 23 cm (nine-inch) rat but Oosterman said: "We will try and match her with another rat but it's not the same as our rat."
She warned the thieves that Sweetie was not always true to her name.
"She is a sweetie with those she loves but she bites people she doesn't like and she could be infectious."
